text:
maria.s: FYI customer acme-inc is seeing a cascade of 502s when creating guest payment records. Happening during heavy batch writes. trace_id=trace-9a8b7c
liam: Can you paste a minimal curl the customer is running and any headers? Also the trace id from the edge.
maria.s: Sure — sample request from support ticket:
```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/guest/pay
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED'
  -H 'X-Tenant: acme-inc'
  -H 'X-Request-ID: trace-9a8b7c'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  --data '{"user":{"id":"guest-1234"},"payment":{"method":"card","amount":1}}'
```
Response: 502 from edge, no useful body. Upstream trace shows billing-write returning 503/timeout then edge -> 502.
neha: infra-bot alerted earlier: "edge-gateway: 502 surge detected in frontdoor pool — 03:12 UTC — 6.8% error rate — affected tenant acme-inc". @frank any backend visibility?
infra-bot: alert id=alert-7765, CPU spike on billing-write pool 03:11:52 UTC, DB write latency > 500ms, auto-throttle triggered.
frank: Looking now — billing write service saw a DB throttling event for the tenant's partition. A recent tenant migration increased write amplification; DB started returning transient errors, we propagated 503. Investigating a quick rollback of the migration.
maria.s: Customer says it correlates with large metadata in the request (hosted app sends big payload). Reproduces locally when payload > ~12KB.
liam: Can you repro with http2 flags? Try:
```bash
curl --http2 -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/guest/pay \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED' \
  -H 'X-Tenant: acme-inc' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: trace-9a8b7c' \
  -H 'Connection: keep-alive' \
  --data-binary @large_payload.json
```
We want to see if keepalive + large body causes upstream conn window exhaustion causing envoy to return 502.
neha: Captured a raw edge trace for trace-9a8b7c: envoy -> billing-proxy: upstream reset, then envoy responds 502 to client. No upstream 200s. Stack indicates DB write timeouts inside billing service.
olivia: Quick mitigation suggestion: ask customer to retry with exponential backoff or split into smaller requests. Also we can enable short-term fallback route to dedicated billing pool for acme-inc to reduce load on shared partition.
liam: Workaround we used in a separate tenant incident: set header `x-rw-fallback: dedicated` (internal flag) to route to reserved path for a minute while backends stabilize. Not a permanent fix but reduces 502 surface.
frank: Patch: rolling back the tenant migration, increasing DB write provision for acme-inc; should reduce 5xx within ~5-10m. Also adding a short circuit in billing-proxy to return 503 earlier rather than letting envoy time out to 502.
maria.s: Can we also add a targeted alert: billing 5xx rate > 2% for > 1m for any tenant triggers paging? Right now alerts are at service-wide level, noisy.
neha: Will add tenant-scoped 5xx rate dashboard and an alert rule. Also adding a temporary rule to flip throttles per-tenant when DB errors spike so we degrade gracefully.
maria.s: I'll update the customer ticket with repro steps and suggest split requests + exponential backoff. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
liam: Follow-ups: capture full edge proxy logs for trace-9a8b7c and send to frank for postmortem. Also recommend support add curl sample with `--http2` when filing.
frank: Got the logs and started a postmortem draft. Leaving a note to consider provisioning guardrails for tenant migrations.
maria.s: Closing loop for now — customer applied reduced batch size and errors dropped. Will reopen if we see recurrence.
